doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Roy Eldridge and Sonny Stitt in Milwaukee
summary: Stitt gets Ware the Roy Eldridge job after Slappy's after-hours sessions; they play two weeks in Milwaukee while Charlie Ventura is down the street.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Sonny Stitt was in the band?

Yeah, well, see, Roy come to Chicago looking for a band, and he knew Stitt was hanging around, because I think that's where Eckstein's band broke up was in Chicago; in fact, they did break up in Chicago. They played the Regal Theatre and that was the end of it. But Stitt was around then, and he told me one night, it was at a little after hours place, all the musicians used to come and jam,

called 'Slappy's' on 29th and Indiana. And after I got off my job downtown on Sunday, I'd pull by there. You know, and we just jammed all morning, to at least 1 or 2 o'clock in the afternoon. And Stitt would be down there, and he says to me, 'Man, I got a job for you if you want it.' He had [Don Rail] Anderson drumming, a pianist named Willie Jones, who, Willie incidentally, was playing that locked-hand style, and still is, Big Willie Jones -- he said you're going to work with Roy Eldridge. Elton: Roy had 2 weeks up in Milwaukee, and he asked me did I want it, and I said, 'Yeah.'
So we bought uniform jackets at least, and we went to Milwaukee with Roy Elton.
What kind of things were you playing?

Oh, we were playing beautiful things. We were playing music, and Stitt was playing -- you might say we were young turks, and we were able to play any kind of music, but we added on what they would call 'bebop' if you want to call it that. Right down the street, Charlie Ventura had his band, and had this vocalist Buddy Stewart with him, Kai Winding, Shelly Manne -- I think Buddy Clark was on bass, and we were doing pretty good. During that time, this pianist, Heywood, was in town, playing music up in Milwaukee, you know.
